name: Asia Society Hong Kong Center
notes: Asia Society Hong Kong Center, Admiralty: the former British Army explosives magazine compound (1840s-1860s) on the hillside above Justice Drive, restored, with Tod Williams Billie Tsien's additions (2012): a long, low pavilion of dark grey-green stone with glazed fronts and a roof garden with a pool, and the zig-zag bridge under its folded roof that crosses the wooded ravine to the old compound; the magazines' whitewashed buildings with pitched tiled roofs and their blast walls; subtropical woods. Refined 6 Oct 2026 from published descriptions and the ground file's OpenStreetMap outlines, not photographs (none reachable): the outlines show a block about 28 by 60 m running north-south west of the point (read as the pavilion; OpenStreetMap counts it six storeys, likely measured from the hill below) and a north-south strip of low buildings east of a path (the compound), so the pavilion was moved about 20 m west and 22 m north onto the first and widened to 24 m, and the three old buildings re-set end to end along the strip (Magazine A, the laboratory, the GG magazine), with the bridge landing at the strip's north end; Justice Drive along the north, more trees on the slope. On its outlines 10% before, 66% now. Still guessed: every dimension, which outline is which building, the bridge's plan (drawn in right-angled zig-zags), the roofs and the terrain (two terraces).
